articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully launches toward Mars's moon Phobos in a landmark Japanese space exploration achievement. This mission will study the Martian moon system and collect samples for return to Earth.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo, the joint ESA-JAXA Mercury exploration mission, celebrates a major milestone in its eight-year journey to study the innermost planet. The spacecraft continues its pioneering mission to unlock Mercury's secrets.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch aboard a Japanese H3 rocket toward Mars's moon system. This ambitious endeavor promises groundbreaking discoveries about the Martian moons and their origins.

articles.title: Smithsonian scientists just recreated the first 2 billion years of the Universe
articles.description: Scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe ever made, offering an extraordinary new glimpse into the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. Called Lumina, the groundbreaking simulation recreates the universe’s first 2 billion years, showing how dark matter, gas, and radiation interacted to give rise to the earliest stars, galaxies, and black holes.
articles.summary: Smithsonian scientists create one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe's first 2 billion years, providing unprecedented insights into cosmic origins.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers detect three actively feeding supermassive black holes within a single galaxy from the universe's dawn, challenging formation models and revealing unexpected cosmic complexity.

articles.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.
articles.summary: Astronomers present compelling evidence for the first moon ever discovered beyond our Solar System, a potentially historic finding that expands our understanding of exoplanetary systems.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA JPL celebrates 90 years of innovation with ambitious future plans including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Mars helicopters that will revolutionize space exploration.

articles.title: Drei Raketen, drei Raumschiffe: So irre plant die NASA Artemis 3
articles.description: Voraussichtlich im Sommer 2027 soll mit Artemis 3 eine komplexe Testmission starten. In der Erdumlaufbahn soll das Zusammenspiel von drei verschiedenen Raumfahrzeugen erprobt werden, um den Betrieb künftiger Mondlandefähren vorzubereiten.(Weiter lesen)
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis 3 mission is planned for summer 2027, featuring a complex assembly of three rockets and spacecraft in Earth orbit to advance lunar exploration.

articles.title: Webb Sees Turbulent Star Nursery
articles.description: In this Webb image released on Oct. 22, 2026, we see a turbulent cauldron of star formation filled with dense clumps of gas. This region is named N159 and is located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This region has a lower metallicity […]
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captures a stunning image of a turbulent star-forming region filled with dense clumps of gas and dust. This observation reveals the dynamic processes of stellar birth in unprecedented detail.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media to Crew Completion of Yearlong Mars Simulation
articles.description: The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health and performance data collected from the simulation can help NASA develop methods […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates the completion of a yearlong Mars habitat simulation with four volunteer crew members, advancing human preparation for future Mars missions. This milestone demonstrates progress toward crewed interplanetary exploration.

articles.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description:
Image:
			Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.summary: An awe-inspiring image shows stars actively forming within a nebulous cauldron of gas and cosmic material. This stellar nursery demonstrates the ongoing creation of new stars throughout our galaxy.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope makes a remarkable discovery by identifying its first previously unknown comet. This achievement highlights the telescope's powerful capabilities for advancing astronomical knowledge.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Solar Orbiter spacecraft tracks and studies mysterious magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind near the Sun. These S-shaped kinks in the magnetic field reveal new insights into solar physics and space weather.

articles.title: The Rubin Observatory Finds Its First Dwarf Planet Candidate
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory found a distant Solar System object before its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time even got started. The object is a dwarf planet candidate named 2026 ED138, and if confirmed, it will be one of the largest dwarf planets beyond Neptune. It may be up to 1500 km in diameter.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has identified its first dwarf planet candidate in the distant Solar System before officially beginning its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time.

articles.title: Glowing Salt Crystals Tracked Radiation Aboard Artemis I
articles.description: There weren’t any humans strapped into the bucket seats of the Orion spacecraft for the Artemis I mission. But there were two anthropomorphic mannequins made to mimic human bone and soft tissue, but also equipped with hundreds of radiation sensors spread throughout their body as part of the Matroshka AstroRad Radiation Experiment. A recent paper led by Paweł Bilski of the Institute for Nuclear Physics of the Polish Academy of Sciences, and published in the journal Radiation Measurements, reports on the results of that experiment, including the operation of a new type of long-term passive radiation monitor made of lithium.
articles.summary: Glowing salt crystals aboard the uncrewed Artemis I mission tracked radiation exposure, providing valuable data for human lunar exploration.

articles.title: NASA Systems Engineering Team Details HWO Mission Architecture
articles.description: Finding an Earth-like world beyond the solar system is the Holy Grail of exoplanet research, and the field has experienced incredible technological advancements in searching for and identifying exoplanets since the first exoplanet was discovered in 1995. This includes both ground- and space-based telescopes, specifically the powerful James Webb Space Telescope. However, directly imaging exoplanets remains elusive, primarily due to the enormous technological challenge of imaging a point of light so far away.
articles.summary: NASA's systems engineering team has detailed the architecture for the Habitable Worlds Observatory mission, a groundbreaking effort to discover Earth-like exoplanets.

articles.title: Massive Stellar Collisions Could Explain Early Supermassive Black Holes
articles.description: Dense stellar environments were common in the early Universe. These environments fostered more numerous stellar collisions, and some of those would've been mergers that formed very massive stars. Those stars would've exploded as supernovae, becoming massive black holes, the potential seeds for today's supermassive black holes.
articles.summary: Dense stellar environments in the early Universe may have fostered massive stellar collisions that explain the existence of supermassive black holes observed in ancient galaxies.

articles.title: First light: Hera resolves two asteroids instead of one
articles.description: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft for planetary defense has resolved its two target asteroids separately for the first time, revealing the binary nature of the Didymos system, currently some 197 million km (122 million miles) away from Earth.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: ESA's Hera spacecraft achieves first light by successfully resolving its two target asteroids as separate objects, marking a major milestone in planetary defense technology.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis I mission reveals surprising radiation levels near the Moon
articles.description: NASA’s Artemis I mission has revealed that cosmic radiation near the Moon is higher than in Earth orbit, but not by as much as scientists might expect. Tiny experimental detectors also uncovered surprising details about how radiation passes through the human body, offering valuable insights for future lunar exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis I mission provides crucial new data on cosmic radiation environments near the Moon, informing safety protocols for future human lunar exploration.

articles.title: James Webb discovers a scorching lava planet with a “giant sunscreen”
articles.description: A scorching lava planet 280 light-years away has surprised astronomers by apparently maintaining a thick atmosphere despite conditions that should have stripped it away billions of years ago. James Webb Space Telescope observations suggest that TOI-561 b reflects about 75% of incoming starlight, possibly because of mineral clouds that act like a giant sunscreen. The planet may also be continually replenishing its atmosphere through gases released from a global ocean of molten rock.
articles.summary: James Webb Space Telescope discovers a distant lava planet that mysteriously retains a thick atmosphere despite extreme temperatures, challenging current atmospheric retention models.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples from NASA's asteroid Bennu mission reveal 4.5-billion-year-old secrets that are rewriting our understanding of Solar System formation and early planetary development.

articles.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
articles.description: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.
articles.summary: Using advanced balloon-borne telescope technology, astronomers uncover a complex magnetic web above the Sun's quiet regions, revealing surprising hidden complexity in solar magnetism.

articles.title: Astronomers found a mysterious object beyond Neptune, and it could be a new dwarf planet
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered a suspected dwarf planet beyond Neptune's orbit. If confirmed, it would be the sixth known dwarf planet in our solar system.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory discovers a suspected dwarf planet beyond Neptune's orbit, potentially adding a new member to our Solar System's distant outer reaches.

articles.title: Black holes can split in two — but only if they spin at extreme speeds
articles.description: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. New research suggests that the opposite may happen too: single black holes may split in two.
articles.summary: Researchers discover that black holes can split into two separate black holes under extreme spinning conditions, expanding our understanding of black hole dynamics beyond simple mergers.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.description: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.summary: Astronomers unveil new insights into a rare 'string of pearls' supernova remnant and its companion zombie star, revealing secrets about stellar death and cosmic recycling.

articles.title: Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? [8:42]
articles.description: A leading theory proposes that ancient Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? | 8:42 VideoFr…
articles.summary: Scientists explore the Giant Impact Hypothesis, which proposes that a massive collision between early Earth and a planet-sized object led to the Moon's formation.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers confirm the first detection of a microblazar, a smaller cousin of high-energy blazars, expanding our understanding of compact cosmic objects.

articles.title: Überholmanöver im All: Japan will beim Mars-Wettlauf gewinnen
articles.description:
Seit Jahren arbeiten verschiedene Raumfahrtnationen daran, erstmals Gesteinsproben vom Mars zur Erde zu transportieren. Während deren Vorhaben ins Stocken geraten sind, wählt ein weiterer Akteur nun eine indirekte Route mit eigenen Risiken.
weiterlesen auf t3…
articles.summary: Japan accelerates its Mars sample return mission efforts, joining the international race to bring Martian rocks back to Earth in this exciting era of Mars exploration.

articles.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5043-5049: Preparing to Drill at ‘Nazca’
articles.description: Written by Lucy Lim, Planetary Scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 16, 2026 Following the Basque Lakes drill campaign, Curiosity has returned to a spot just a few meters away from the “Chiu Chiu” block to conduct our next drill campaign. “Chiu Chiu” itself wasn’t a good candidate for […]
articles.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover continues its groundbreaking exploration of Mars, preparing to drill at a new site called 'Nazca.' The mission demonstrates ongoing scientific discovery on the Red Planet.
